title: Does Training on Future Data Pay? Look-Ahead Bias in Forecasting with Pretrained Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.20554v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We examine whether post-origin training information inflates the measured accuracy and economic value of financial forecasts. We evaluate five sets of financial time-series foundation models, each comprising independently trained annual vintages under U.S., global, and factor-augmented training environments, across 14 equity markets and four forecast horizons. Rolling comparisons vary the annual vintage for a fixed forecast; fixed-vintage comparisons hold the vintage fixed as target windows move across its training cutoff. Each alternative forecast is paired with an origin-aligned point-in-time (PIT) benchmark using identical numerical histories and inference protocols. In the U.S.-trained reference environment, post-origin vintages materially revise informative PIT forecasts but generally reduce accuracy in both designs. Pooled rolling comparisons yield higher mean squared forecast errors in 18 of 20 U.S. model-set-horizon combinations.

translated_title: 在未来数据上训练是否有回报？预训练模型预测中的前视偏差
translated_abstract: 我们研究了在预测发布时点之后的训练信息是否会夸大金融预测所测得的精度和经济价值。我们评估了五套金融时间序列基础模型，每套模型包含在美国、全球以及因子增强训练环境下独立训练的年度版本（vintages），覆盖14个股票市场和四个预测期限。滚动比较在固定预测目标的情况下更换年度版本；固定版本比较则在目标窗口跨越模型训练截止日期时保持版本不变。每个替代预测都与一个使用相同数值历史和推断协议、与发布时点对齐的时点（PIT）基准进行配对。在以美国训练环境为参照的设置中，事后版本会实质性地修订原本具有信息量的时点预测，但在两种设计下通常都会降低预测精度。汇总的滚动比较显示，在20个美国模型集-期限组合中，有18个出现了更高的均方预测误差。
tldr: 该论文通过构建与发布时点对齐的时点基准，发现用未来数据（事后版本）训练的预训练模型并不能提升金融预测精度，反而通常降低精度，揭示了预训练模型预测中存在的前视偏差问题。
en_tdlr: By constructing origin-aligned point-in-time benchmarks, this paper shows that training pretrained models on future data does not improve—and typically degrades—financial forecast accuracy, revealing look-ahead bias in pretrained-model forecasting.
